- When sentiment is strongly positive (≥0.7) in recent days, model tends to overestimate prices; adjust forecast downward by 1–3% for next period.  
- When sentiment is strongly negative (≤-0.3), model underestimates; increase forecast by 1–3% to account for potential rebound.  
- Model consistently underestimates prices in the first 5–7 days of a new 30-day horizon; apply a 0.5–1.5% upward bias to early periods.  
- After a sharp price spike (≥5% from prior peak), model often overshoots; reduce forecast by 2–5% in the immediate follow-up period.  
- Model shows persistent mean reversion bias: if 3–5 consecutive days show downward trend, forecast should be slightly above recent lows to avoid underestimating rebound.  
- When sentiment history shows alternating high/low swings, model tends to lag; add 1–2 days of lagged sentiment influence to forecast adjustment.
